title: Hydrogen bonds and Trouton's rule
question: Per pure liquid (one reading nearest 25 °C, plausible ΔS only): is the mean of ds_implied higher for hbond = O–H donor than for hbond = no H-bond donor?

issues.text: Whether a liquid hydrogen-bonds is not a field: it is read from the SMILES with a pattern for O–H and N–H groups.
issues.fix: The hbond category in compounds; check the O–H list by hand (it holds water-free acids, glycols, phenols).

issues.text: Donors also differ in size and polarity, and acids dimerise in the vapour, which lowers ΔS.
issues.fix: Compare at similar boiling points (tb_k) and report carboxylic acids apart.

issues.text: ΔS from one reading far below Tb mixes Trouton's constant with the temperature dependence of ΔH_vap.
issues.fix: Compare classes at the same x = Tb/T − 1, or add a second reading per liquid.

alternatives.question: Is ds_implied higher for N–H donors (amines) than for liquids with no donor?
alternatives.why: Drills into the weaker donor class (27 liquids).

alternatives.question: Does ds_implied rise with x = Tb/T − 1 among non-donors, as Watson's correlation predicts?
alternatives.why: Separates the temperature dependence of ΔH_vap from hydrogen bonding.

alternatives.question: Do donor/non-donor pairs form azeotropes more often than non-donor pairs?
alternatives.why: Expands to mixtures, the distillation consequence.

hypotheses.statement: Liquids with an O–H donor have a higher implied entropy of vaporisation than liquids with no hydrogen-bond donor.
hypotheses.null: The mean ds_implied is the same for both classes.

hypotheses.statement: The boiling point predicts the vapour pressure less well for O–H donors: their log₁₀(reported/predicted) is below zero.
hypotheses.null: log_ratio_fit has the same mean for donors and non-donors.

outcome.concept: Vapour pressure against the boiling-point prediction

concepts.label: Pure substance
concepts.description: A Wikidata item with a SMILES, a vapour pressure at a stated temperature and a normal boiling point.

concepts.label: Entropy of vaporisation
concepts.description: R ln(P0/P)/(Tb/T − 1) from one reading, J/(mol·K).

concepts.label: Hydrogen-bond donor
concepts.description: O–H donor, N–H donor or none, from SMILES patterns.

concepts.label: Distance below the boiling point
concepts.why: A confounder: ΔH_vap changes with temperature.

concepts.label: Carboxylic acid
concepts.description: Acids dimerise in the vapour, lowering ΔS_vap.
concepts.why: A subgroup that behaves against the hypothesis.

strategy.detail: SMILES containing C(=O)O with a terminal O

concepts.label: Measured heat of vaporisation
concepts.description: Calorimetric ΔH_vap at Tb, to test Trouton without the temperature extrapolation.

strategy.detail: NIST Chemistry WebBook or Wikidata P2116, matched on PubChem CID

data.request: Enthalpy of vaporisation at the normal boiling point for the same compounds
data.source: NIST Chemistry WebBook (by CAS/CID); Wikidata P2116 holds only about 24
data.why: Tests Trouton's rule at Tb directly.

method.summary: Mean ds_implied of O–H donors against non-donors, Welch-style with unequal variances; the board's welch step gives the classical t as a check.

steps.title: Readings from Wikidata
steps.detail: Vapour pressure with temperature and boiling point with pressure, units as entered (vp).

steps.title: Hydrogen-bond donors
steps.detail: hbond from SMILES patterns for O–H and N–H.

steps.title: Compare the means
steps.detail: ds_implied by hbond, plausible readings only (welch, by_group).

steps.title: Donors against non-donors
steps.detail: Interval of the difference above 5 J/(mol·K)?

caveats: Wikidata readings are rounded safety-sheet values; 11 imply impossible ΔS and are excluded.
A single constant ΔH between T and Tb is an approximation; the class difference is partly a difference in x.
Acids dimerise in the vapour and pull the O–H class down.
The donor class is a SMILES pattern; a few groups (oximes, thiols) are not handled.
